newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan lawmakers to visit Shanghai in January.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan lawmakers to visit Shanghai in January.

text.p: Taiwanese lawmakers plan to visit Shanghai to promote ties, despite their government's freeze on cooperative initiatives with China, an organiser said on Tuesday.
The move also comes after Beijing's successful courtship of South Africa in which Pretoria last week vowed to sever ties with Taipei in favour of Beijing by the end of 1997.

More than 20 lawmakers from the ruling and opposition parties would visit air and sea transport facilities in Shanghai between January 2 and 5, an aide to ruling Nationalist Party lawmaker Tina Pan, who organised the tour, told Reuters.
The group was also scheduled to meet officials and businessmen to seek possible cooperation, the aide said.
"The visit has nothing to do with politics," the aide said.
Taipei last week criticised Beijing's apparent diplomatic coup over South Africa as an uncompromising push to drive Taiwan from the international stage.
Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council said on Friday it would not move to further boost economic links with China in the near future.
South Africa, Taipei's biggest ally, is one of the only 30 states recognising Taiwan's exiled Republic of China.
China has regarded Taiwan as a rebel-held province not entitled to international recognition since a civil war separated them in 1949.
The aide said the group did not rule out the possibility of discussing direct transport links with China which have been banned by Nationalist Taiwan since 1949.
